corrections: 1. Registration under the Voluntary and Humanitarian Work (Organization) Act 2006 is handled by the Humanitarian Aid Commission (HAC) Registrar General, not the 'Ministry of Culture & Information'. 2. HAC fees set under Council of Ministers resolution 3/2023 were SDG 600,000 (~US$1,050) for international NGO registration and SDG 400,000 (~US$700) annual renewal, so the ~$100-300 range applies only to national NGOs at best.

1. Law 19/2001 is still being applied. A High Judicial Council legal opinion of 8 March 2023 treated post-2011 NGOs as unlawful, and PM Circular No. 7 (21 March 2023) requires NGOs to regularise under Law 19/2001 through the Decree 138 registration committee/Civil Society Commission. This should replace the reference to the '2013 circulars'.

1. Law 12-06 of 12 January 2012 was not formally amended in 2020. The 2020 Constitution (Art. 53) only changed the constitutional basis to a declaration regime. The 2025 replacement bill was still a draft as of late 2025, so drop 'amended 2020'.

1. The governing text is Decree-Law 2011-88 of 24 September 2011, which repealed Law 59-154 of 7 November 1959. The notes' claim that 'governing text is Decree-Law 59-154 of 1959' is wrong. 2. '13+' in the decree is the minimum age for members (founders must be at least 16), not a minimum member count. 3. An organic bill to replace Decree-Law 88 (filed October 2023) was still pending in the ARP committee as of mid-2026 and has not been adopted.

1. Cooperatives are governed by Law 112-12 (promulgated by Dahir 1-14-189 of 21 November 2014, amended by Law 74-16), not 'Law 19-00'. The association law citation (Dahir 1-58-376 of 1958 as amended by Law 75-00 of 2002) is correct.

1. The registrar is the Authority for Civil Society Organizations (ACSO) under the Ministry of Justice, not a 'Civil Society Registry Commission'. 2. There is no 'CSO Proclamation 1259/2021'. The governing law remains Proclamation No. 1113/2019. A restrictive amendment bill was circulated in mid-2025, but I found no evidence it has been enacted. 3. Under Proc. 1113/2019 a local organization may be formed by Ethiopians, foreigners resident in Ethiopia, or both. Only non-resident foreigners are excluded, so 'no' holds for a remote founder.

1. The federal 'NGO Act 2019' is still described by ICNL as a draft bill (the cited consortium PDF is the Nov 2019 draft). I found no evidence that it was signed into law. Federal NGO registration is handled administratively by the Ministry of Planning, Investment and Economic Development (and the Ministry of Interior), not 'FMOO'. Describe the federal law as draft/pending.

1. The governing law is Law No. 43/2010 on Welfare (Charitable) Non-Governmental Organisations (National and International), not 'Presidential Decree No. 82/11'. 2. The registering body is the Ministry of National Planning and Development, which is the sole body mandated to register national and international NGOs. It is not an interior/social-affairs ministry. Ministry guidance says registration takes up to 2 weeks once complete, and registration must be renewed periodically.

1. The last published RRC schedule (May 2017) set annual registration at US$500 for national NGOs and US$3,500 for international NGOs. Registration fees were waived in 2018, with renewal/admin fees of US$200 (national) and US$1,000 (international). The $300-600 range fits national NGOs only.

1. The local regime is the Associations Act 2022 (Act 8 of 2022), which repealed the Registration of Associations Act (Cap 201). It came into operation on 14 August 2023 (SI 54 of 2023), except for parts of s.25 and s.28(1), which were suspended by the Associations (Amendment) Act 2023. The notes' claim that 'NPO Act Cap. 741 (NPO Act 2013) is the current local regime' is unsupported and should be removed. The Foundations Act 2009 route is unaffected.

1. The foundation statute is the Foundations Act 2012 (Act 8 of 2012), not 'Foundations Act 2016' as shown in the entity-types column. Foundations are registered with the Registrar of Foundations, under FSC oversight.

1. The non-profit company vehicle is a Section 42 licensed company under the Companies Act 2017. References to a 'Sec 21 company' are wrong and should read Section 42. 2. The licensing procedure, guidebook and checklist are now set out in the Companies Regulations 2024 (regs 4-5), which supersede the 2018 regulations cited. The licence is issued for 3 years and is renewable, and incorporation must follow within 60 days of licence issue.

1. The Foreign Donations (Voluntary Activities) Regulation Ordinance 1978 was replaced by the Foreign Donations (Voluntary Activities) Regulation Act 2016 (Act No. 8 of 2016). Registration of foreign-funded NGOs is with the NGO Affairs Bureau, not BIDA. 2. The '1961 NGO Act' is the Voluntary Social Welfare Agencies (Registration and Control) Ordinance 1961, administered by the Department of Social Services. I could not verify the two-thirds Bangladeshi-citizen board rule attributed to its s.3.

1. The Trusts Ordinance is Cap. 87 (Ordinance No. 9 of 1917), not Cap. 72. Charitable trusts may be incorporated by Ministerial order under s.114. Sri Lanka has no 'Commissioner of Charities'. Registration and administration sit with the Registrar-General / Ministry of Justice.

1. There is no general 'Trust Act 2000'. Private and charitable trusts are governed by the National Civil Code 2074 (2017), ss.314-351. The Nepal Trust Act 2064 (2008) only concerns former royal property. 2. Under Civil Code s.316(4)-(5) and s.320(3), a foreign settlor may establish a (non-religious) trust, but at least one-third of trustees must be Nepali citizens with permanent residence in Nepal, and the foreigner must remit movable property worth at least US$1 million within 3 months. The trust route is therefore not a low-barrier expat path. 3. An NGO under the Associations Registration Act 2034 (1977) requires at least 7 founders who are Nepali citizens, not '5 of 7'.
